description: A serene, organic bathroom vanity in warm sand plaster with a minimalist Japandi-California sensibility. The wall is finished in heavily textured warm sand or stucco plaster with a rough, uneven hand-applied surface, the color falling between pale gold and warm taupe. A large free-form organic mirror with a thin curved frame in warm antiqued brass hangs at standing eye height, its irregular silhouette echoing natural stone shapes. Below the mirror, a thick live-edge wood vanity slab in warm honey oak serves as the counter, its raw organic edge visible. On this counter surface sit three pump bottles — one amber glass and two in matte neutral tones — a neatly folded soft linen hand towel in a warm grid check pattern in sage and cream, a small ceramic cup holding a bud vase with one dried stem, and a small decorative ceramic tray with a few pebble-like objects. A round vessel sink in textured natural travertine or light stone sits to the left. The wall-mounted faucet set is in a warm matte brass finish. The room receives soft natural light from a partially visible window at upper left. A warm glow flanks the mirror on the right side, washing the plaster texture with honeyed illumination. The overall palette is warm neutral — sand plaster, honey wood, warm brass. The mood is serene and spa-like. Camera is at standing eye level, centered on the vanity mirror in a near-symmetrical composition with a normal lens.
